correctness.rationale: Outside finitely many primes the split model reduces with all four two-torsion points rational and distinct. A finite abelian 2-primary group with exactly four points killed by 2 has order divisible by 8 iff it contains an order-four point, equivalently a rational half of a nonzero 2-torsion point. Applying Bekker–Zarhin gives the three ordered-root tests (ma=mc=1), (a=mb=1), and (b=c=1). The positive gap squareclasses give a totally real multiquadratic field, so adjoining i supplies an independent sign. Chebotarev yields equal frequencies for the permissible patterns. Independently generating all relation subspaces by spans and using the number of successful m-signs (2,2,2,0,1,1,1,1 in negative-sign mask order) reproduces the complete 16-row calculation. The four proposed examples have relation spaces {0,3,4,7}, {0}, {0,1} and the full space. For the D(8) model the nonsquare classes are 238 and 2, independent since 238/2=119 is nonsquare, while the third difference is 1024; the test succeeds in 6 of the 8 allowed patterns. A separate matrix-based census also confirms the spectrum.
residual_risks: The finite-field sign expressions are used only where the displayed roots reduce to distinct finite elements; the exclusions are finite and harmless for natural density.
The proof need not realize all 16 abstract relation spaces; it realizes every density value.

evidence: Rouse–Zureick-Brown classify all 1208 exact non-CM 2-adic images, with realized representatives identified by the companion tables. Lozano-Robledo supplies corresponding classifications for CM and explicit 2-adic generators, e.g. for j=1728.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These are stronger input than just a general existence-of-density theorem. In particular the explicit CM and non-CM images determine the same local order test after projection. Independently, in every image including CM, complex conjugation yields A with trace 1 and determinant 0 (det(g)=−1 and g has eigenvalue 1); this single necessary condition suffices to check that the four non-CM values exhaust the universal set.

The D(8) model and its bounded reductions are already in arXiv:2610.03121v1; its density is not stated there. Gekeler's 11/48 for divisibility by eight is an average over varying curves, not the fixed-curve claim.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: In the trivial mod-2 kernel, g=I+2A modulo 4. The mod-8 divisibility test depends only on A because the determinant is homogeneous of degree two. Chebotarev therefore counts exactly the singular A in the additive image, which is the same event as halving one of the nonzero 2-torsion points.

originality.rationale: The exact spectrum is a short, explicitly verified projection of prior results, not merely work in a similar area. The published Frobenius determinant formula gives the prime density from the exact mod-4 image when mod 2 is trivial: for g=I+2A, det(I−g)≡4det(A) mod 8. Reducing the realized groups in the Rouse–Zureick-Brown companion data to mod 4, retaining precisely the groups trivial mod 2, and counting singular elements gives the four stated values, each already attained among their non-CM representatives. For the CM extension the same published determinant test applies; all possible matrix spaces containing the prescribed complex-conjugation type give no extra value. The gap-character proof is a transparent alternative calculation, but the frozen claim of a distinct exact spectrum is covered as a consequence of stronger prior data and the standard test. No claim is made that the same boxed wording or the specific D(8) density appeared verbatim.
residual_risks: No assertion that an earlier article printed exactly these fractions together, used the same four explicit witnesses, or named the same D(8) density. The failure is based on the actual deterministic implication and reproduction from prior exact mathematical inputs, not on those stronger bibliographic claims.

value.rationale: The family and invariant are mathematically natural, and the gap proof gives a convenient way to compute the density without looking up an image. But the frozen finding presents the exact spectrum and a single-model evaluation as the new mathematical contribution. The four values and their attainment already come from a short projection of the exact prior images and the standard local test; the example is one elementary specialization of the known halving criterion. No separate structural or general result is proved that survives this overlap as a valuable new claim.
residual_risks: The self-contained squareclass presentation remains useful exposition; the decision concerns the contribution of the frozen claim, not the pedagogical utility of that proof.
